what: In the hero, an oval photo window inside a frame grows with scroll — its diameter starts at 332 (for a 1600 design width) and grows .2 per 1px of scroll, the frame panel grows at the same ratio around the same point (the frame center), and the background only approaches at a .02 ratio. Both blur .005px for each unit of growth, so the photo fills the screen as if sucked into the frame. After 2 screens the panel disappears in .75s

options.base: Initial window diameter (design width in px), default 332 — 280 on phones
options.design: Design width (px) — scaled down in proportion to the panel width, default 1600 (phone 390)
options.rate: Diameter increase per 1px of scroll, default .2
options.bg: Increase per 1px of background scroll, default .02
options.blur: Blur per 1px of added diameter (px), default .005
options.until: Past this number of screens it gets is-fx-past (fades out), default 2
options.x · y: Window and axis center (% of panel), default 50.69 · 40 — original 811/1600 · 403px
options.[data-fx-part=window]: Photo layer to be cropped into an ellipse
options.[data-fx-part=frame]: Framed picture layer (grows while blurring) — optional

use: …
note: For a hero where the panel sticks to the top of the screen — counts from the very start of the window document scroll (or the data-fx-scroller panel)

from.where: index.html .bk-mv (original RS(): --ellipse-x/y = width/1600 × (332+.2y)/2 · ×402/332, --frame-scale (332+.2y)/332, --bg-scale (332+.02y)/332, --blur (.2y)×.005px, y > On 2 screens, is-active fades out in .75s, 10ms throttle)
